text.p: Belgian shares ended lower on Friday as European markets slipped on profit taking ahead of the results of France's elections and ongoing fears about Europe's single currency project.

However, Brussels Bel-20 blue chip index .BFX weathered the storm better than most, slipping 0.44 percent to 2,247.77 points despite the fact the Dow .DJI in New York lost more than one percent in early trade.
Dealers said there was still buying interest in selected stocks and company news originating from annual general meetings was sustaining interest in the market.
"What happens Monday will depend on the French elections," Generale Bank analyst Luc Van der Elst said.
Koramic, which held its annual meeting on Wednesday ended up 20 francs at 2,075 francs after hitting a new all-time high of 2,100 francs mid-session.

Cobepa rose 12 francs to 1,510 francs as the stock continued to benefit from a reshuffle in Belgiums corporate world last week that has led to a reappraisal of some holding companies. However, holding company CNP/NPM ended 30 francs lower at 2,570 francs despite news it also wants to narrow the discount between its share and net asset value.
After the close of trade, CNP/NPM said the company's net asset value per share was 3,195 francs on May 29. It was the first in what it said would be a weekly statement on its NAV.

Retailers were also actively traded, although one dealer said there had been no special news to animate their shares. GIB rose 25 francs, or 1.62 percent, to 1,570 francs. Delhaize rose 15 francs, or 0.86 percent, at 1,755 francs.
Meanwhile, holding company Synergia ended its first week on Brussels Euro.NM market at 618 francs, 4.9 percent below its IPO price, but up from the week's low of 582 francs.
